text:
Iona: FYI we discovered a couple of metric/name collisions between runtime and infra when trying to wire up new dashboards for rollouts. Can we align on a small ontology before we start adding panels?

Mike: +1. Can you paste what you found?

Iona: quick dump of what runtime is currently exporting (prom-style) — these collide with infra names or use very high-card labels:

```
# runtime
rwinf_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",model="mpt-7b",tenant_id="acme"} 42
rwinf_request_total{route="/v1/generate",model_version="mpt-7b-q4",region="us-west-2"} 1023
rwinf_token_emitted_total{model="mpt-7b",token_type="word"} 409600
rwinf_kv_cache_hit{prefix="/user/",request_id="abcd-1234"} 512
rwinf_batch_size{route="/v1/generate",batch_id="b345"} 8
```

Iona: infra has metrics like `request_total`, `request_duration_seconds` and they set `instance_id` and `host` labels. We need a consistent prefixing + label policy + cardinality rules.

Sophie: Good catch. My main concern: tenant_id and request_id as labels are huge cardinality. We should never expose raw tenant_id in Prom labels for dashboards.

Rahul: Agree. For tenant identifiers we should use `tenant_tier` (prod/staging/test) or `tenant_hash` (low-cardinality truncated hash) only when necessary. For debugging, we can link traces/exemplars back to request_id instead of making it a label.

Mike: Proposed conventions:
- All metric names prefixed with `rwinf_` for runtime; infra keeps `infra_` or `node_` where appropriate.
- Metric names: snake_case, verbs for counters (`_total`), seconds for durations (`_seconds`), ratio/gauge descriptive names.
- Labels: `service`, `env`, `region`, `model`, `model_variant`, `route`, `deployment`, `instance`
- Avoid: `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `session_id` as labels.

Jess: Can we put an explicit cardinality cap in the schema? e.g., "recommended max unique values per label <= 100" for high-card labels like `model` maybe 50 for `route`?

Sophie: I'd say: routes should be coarse (grouped), e.g., use `route_group` instead of full path. For example `/v1/generate` and `/v1/generate-stream` both map to `generate`. That keeps cardinality low.

Iona: Updated sample mapping for OTel -> Prom labels we want to enforce:
```
# OTel resource attr -> Prom label
service.name -> service
service.instance.id -> instance
deployment.environment -> env
cloud.region -> region
host.name -> host
resource.attributes['redwood.model.name'] -> model
resource.attributes['redwood.model.variant'] -> model_variant
```

Iona: And example standardized metrics for dashboard consumption:
```
rwinf_request_total{service,env,region,model,model_variant,route_group}  <-- counter
rwinf_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service,env,region,model,route_group,le}
rwinf_request_errors_total{service,env,region,model,route_group,error_code}
rwinf_kv_cache_hit_ratio{service,env,model}  <-- gauge (0..1)
rwinf_batch_size_avg{service,env,model,route_group}
rwinf_tokens_emitted_total{service,env,model,model_variant}
```

Rahul: For rollouts UX we need per-model latency p50/p95 and a regression signal. We should export summaries/histogram buckets and also a promql-friendly `rwinf_request_duration_seconds{quantile="p95"}` derived via recording rules in monitoring (not raw quantile in runtime).

Mike: Recording rules owned by monitoring team, runtime should expose histograms + exemplars for traces. Also +1 on not exposing tenant_id.

Jess: Actionable items: Iona to update runtime exporter to new label map, Sophie to update infra exporter to add `rwinf_` prefix where appropriate, Rahul to draft cardinality guidelines + example promql for dashboards, Mike to own a short doc for model labels (model vs model_variant). Who volunteers to PR the schema to the repo?

Iona: I can do the runtime PR. Will avoid `request_id` and change `route`->`route_group`. I will also add a metric that emits `rwinf_model_registration` (gauge) with labels {model,model_variant,env} so console can list active variants without exploding.

Sophie: I'll update infra and check existing dashboards for collisions. I'll also add a migration plan: keep old names for 2 weeks with a translation recording rule.

Rahul: I'll put together the cardinality doc and a short script to scan current TSDB for label cardinalities and flag anything > 200 uniques.

observability-bot: new issue created: OBS-214 "Align rwinf metrics + labels" assigned to Iona, Sophie, Rahul. (link: https://issues.redwood.ai/OBS-214) :eyes:

Mike: Thanks all. Can we sync tomorrow 10am to finalize labels?

Jess: Works for me.

Iona: 👍 added to calendar. I'll post PR link here when it's ready.
